title: Closed-loop, machine learning-driven optimization of reactor yields in reactive carbon electrolyzers
experiments_summary: The study used the AdaCarbon self-driving laboratory platform to optimize reactor yield in a reactive carbon electrolyzer through two main experimental campaigns. Six operating parameters were varied: bicarbonate temperature (25–80°C), bicarbonate concentration (0.5–3.05 M), bicarbonate flow rate (30–200 mL/min), KOH concentration (0.05–3.00 M), KOH flow rate (6–30 mL/min), and total applied current density (50–350 mA/cm²). The automated test cell (ATC) housed a silver gas-diffusion electrode cathode, nickel foam anode, and bipolar membrane, with electrolysis run for 5 minutes per experiment. Gaseous products (CO, CO₂, H₂) were analyzed inline by atmospheric pressure chemical ionization triple-quadrupole mass spectrometry. A Gaussian process regression surrogate model was trained using a fixed-noise formulation, with data normalized and standardized, and the q-noisy expected improvement (qNEI) acquisition function was used to select subsequent experiments. Campaign 1 (reactor yield optimization) began with 12 randomly initialized experiments, followed by 10 optimizer-proposed experiments, 5 researcher-defined experiments, and continued until no improvement was observed over 10 consecutive steps (52 total experiments). Campaign 2 (J_CO optimization) used all data from Campaign 1 as initialization and ran until convergence, using only optimizer-proposed points without researcher-defined experiments. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was applied to the surrogate model outputs to quantify each parameter's influence on reactor yield and J_CO. The ATC was validated against a manually assembled electrolyzer by testing three silver-based cathode gas-diffusion electrodes in triplicate at 100 mA/cm² in both setups, with products quantified by gas chromatography in the manual cell. Additionally, a separate set of experiments tested champion conditions from the reactor yield campaign using realistic alkaline CO₂ capture electrolytes with varying bicarbonate:carbonate ratios at fixed 3 M K⁺ concentration, covering the range from pure carbonate to pure bicarbonate.
